name: Florida

context: FL 340: Cover crops in Florida serve to reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion, and the standard aims for at least 90-percent cover during periods of erosive wind or rain.
FL 380: Florida windbreaks are not widely used, yet wind damage is a leading cause of crop loss; slash pine, red cedar and sugarcane windbreaks are cited.
cover_rules: FL 340: Time cover crop establishment with other practices so cover is adequate; aim for a minimum of 90-percent cover during periods of potentially erosive wind or rainfall.
residue: FL 329: Use wind erosion prediction technology to set the residue needed; do not shred residue after harvest, since shredding makes it more susceptible to movement by wind.
windbreak: FL 380: The protected zone on the leeward side is 10 times the maximum design height (H) of the tallest row at age 20.
seeding: FL 550: Native grass seeding rates are 4-6 lb of PLS/acre for wildlife and 8-12 lb of PLS/acre for livestock; double the rate if broadcasting.
FL 550: Planting native species in the rainy season (June - August) has not proved advantageous mainly due to increased weed competition.
disturbed: FL 342: Perennial critical-area seeding: bahiagrass 50 lb/A, switchgrass 10 lb/A; use a nurse crop with slow-establishing bahiagrass.
FL 342: Only perennial plants suit critical area plantings; planting is not complete until perennial vegetation is established.

coverPlant.text: FL 342: Cool-season nurse crops (oats, rye, wheat, annual ryegrass) are seeded between September and February.

seedWin.text: FL 342: Seed nurse crops between September and February.
